flags.title: BadgerCare+ Does NOT Cover 100-138% FPL (Non-Traditional Expansion)
flags.summary: Wisconsin did NOT take the standard ACA Medicaid expansion. BadgerCare+ covers adults with children to 100% FPL and childless adults to 100% FPL — but adults 100-138% FPL are NOT on Medicaid; they are directed to the ACA marketplace with enhanced premium tax credits. This is a critical routing distinction: a client at 120% FPL asking about Medicaid is ineligible for BadgerCare+ and must be routed to the marketplace (healthcare.gov) with subsidy assistance. Do not assume expansion coverage for this income band.

flags.title: Wisconsin W-2 (TANF) - 60-Month Limit, Tiered Work Requirements, Low Benefit
flags.summary: Wisconsin TANF is called W-2 (Wisconsin Works). It is among the most work-requirement-intensive welfare programs in the country. W-2 has four employment slots: Unsubsidized Employment (no W-2 payment), Trial Employment Match (up to $673/month), Community Service Job (up to $653/month), and W-2 Transitions (up to $608/month for those unable to work full requirements). Standard TANF cash assistance as known in other states does not exist in Wisconsin in the same form. 60-month federal lifetime limit applies.

flags.title: Wisconsin SNAP ABAWD Work Requirements - Active
flags.summary: Wisconsin SNAP ABAWD work requirements are fully active - no statewide waiver. ABAWDs 18-54 must document 80 hours/month qualifying activity. Surface exemptions at intake: disability, caregiving, pregnancy, education enrollment. Note: Wisconsin has a state SNAP drug testing policy for recipients with drug-related felony convictions - surface this context if applicable.

flags.title: Wisconsin Minimum Wage $7.25/hr - Federal Floor Only
flags.summary: Wisconsin pays only the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hr - no state minimum above federal. Milwaukee's attempt to enact a city minimum wage was blocked by Wisconsin courts (state preemption). This is the lowest minimum wage among all states in the region. Wage theft is significant in Wisconsin's food processing, dairy agriculture, and manufacturing sectors.

flags.title: Milwaukee Extreme Racial Segregation - Targeted Resource Routing Essential
flags.summary: Milwaukee is one of the most racially segregated cities in the United States. The Black poverty rate in Milwaukee County exceeds 35%, compared to white poverty rates of approximately 10%. This is not an abstract demographic note - it directly affects resource availability, service quality, and navigation. Organizations serving Milwaukee's North Side (primarily Black) have different capacity, funding, and access than those serving the metro broadly. Always use Milwaukee-specific organizations rather than generic Wisconsin resources for Milwaukee residents.

flags.title: Wisconsin Tribal Nations - 11 Tribes with Major Treaty Rights
flags.summary: Wisconsin has 11 federally recognized tribes with significant reservation land and treaty rights - particularly hunting, fishing, and gathering rights that extend OFF reservation throughout traditional territories under the 1837, 1842, and 1854 treaties. The Voigt Decision (1983) reaffirmed these treaty rights after decades of dispute. Tribal governments provide TANF, housing, health care, and child welfare services to enrolled members. ICWA applies in all child welfare matters involving enrolled members.

flags.title: Fox Valley Hmong and Southeast Asian Community - Language Access Essential
flags.summary: The Fox Valley corridor (Appleton, Green Bay, Oshkosh) and Milwaukee have large Hmong and Lao American communities - among the largest concentrations in the US. English proficiency varies significantly across generations. Hmong-language services are available through: Hmong American Peace Academy Milwaukee, Hmong Wisconsin Chamber of Commerce (Appleton), Fox Valley Hmong Mutual Assistance Association (Appleton 920-560-1300). Federal language access rights apply to all programs receiving federal funding - insist on language access for any client with limited English proficiency.

flags.title: Wisconsin UI Appeal - 21-Day Deadline, Document All Job Separation Facts
flags.summary: Wisconsin UI appeal deadline is 21 days from determination mailing - shorter than Ohio (30 days) and Illinois (30 days). Wisconsin has historically high UI denial rates for job separations involving employee conduct - employers often contest. Document all facts around job separation carefully.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Wisconsin Emergency Detention
flags.message: WI involuntary psychiatric hold law: Wisconsin Emergency Detention. Statutory authority: Wis. Stat. § 51.15. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in WI retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in WI: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Wisconsin Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Wisconsin Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
